description: Canary Palestine listens to water, air, power and health in Gaza and the West Bank, station by station, and says early when something goes quiet.
about: Canary Palestine is an early-warning newsroom for water, air, power and health in Gaza and the West Bank. It listens to named reports, station by station, and says so when a station goes quiet.

lead.headline: Gaza is making a third less drinking water than in mid-September
lead.dek: Repairs cut the line to northern Gaza for most of eight days, the Bani Suheila line was down for two, and the southern desalination plant lost power. Eleven water partners may stop work.
lead.reading_note: drinking water produced 6–12 Oct, against the weekly volume in mid-September
lead.src: OCHA humanitarian situation report of 15 Oct (published 19 Oct), WASH Cluster data

silence.title: Silence is the signal.
silence.say: A canary that stops singing is the warning. When a station has had no public report for weeks, the desk does not fill the gap; it counts the days and asks why.

feature.headline: Five times in two months, settlers have cut al-Masoudiya's power
body: Settlers cut off electricity to the al-Masoudiya area, which belongs to Burqa north-west of Nablus, on Monday 12 October. Local official Dhiyab Hajji told WAFA it was the fifth such cut in a little more than two months, and that attacks rose after an outpost was set up near the area (WAFA, 12 Oct).

In its 25 September report, OCHA recorded that about 65 Palestinians in Al Mas'uddiya remained without electricity for more than 24 hours after settlers reportedly vandalised the community's main electricity cable (OCHA, 25 Sep).
The same week, WAFA reported power cuts by settlers to about 20 homes in Wadi al-A'war east of Hebron (12 Oct) and to single homes in Burin (15 Oct) and Beita (18-20 Oct), all south of Nablus.

cards.headline: Gaza hospitals have none of 44% of their essential medicines
cards.summary: Medical sources in Gaza say 44 per cent of essential medicines are at zero stock and 54 per cent of medical consumables are unavailable, including insulin pens, chemotherapy drugs and kidney-transplant immunosuppressants.
cards.src: Medical sources in Gaza via WAFA · 8 Oct

cards.headline: Before the rains, 950,000 displaced people live where floods reach
cards.summary: OCHA says some 950,000 displaced people live in sites at medium to high flood risk, over 400,000 at high risk. Available supplies could partially help only 18 per cent of the 294,250 families needing winter shelter assistance.

cards.headline: Settlers pour concrete at al-Himma spring
cards.summary: Settlers continued bulldozing and enlarging al-Himma spring in the northern Jordan Valley on 7 October, rights activist Aref Daraghmeh told WAFA, bringing a concrete mixer and pouring concrete as part of works to take control of the spring and deny Palestinians its use.
cards.src: Aref Daraghmeh, rights activist via WAFA · 7 Oct

stations.subject: Drinking-water production
stations.what: drinking water produced 6–12 Oct against mid-September: two-thirds of the volume.

stations.subject: Seawater desalination plants
stations.what: of Gaza's people rely on trucked drinking water; the two southern plants are at their lowest output.

stations.subject: Water samples, chlorine
stations.what: of August's 938 samples were below the WHO chlorine level. No September figures since.

stations.subject: Flood risk before the rains
stations.what: people live in sites at medium to high risk of flooding; over 400,000 at high risk.

stations.subject: Wastewater and stormwater
stations.what: people served by wastewater lines repaired in September; the Sheikh Radwan pump station was at 30% in mid-September.

stations.subject: Water lines and springs
stations.what: on water in 16 days: Atouf pipeline destroyed (29 Sep), concrete poured at al-Himma spring (7 Oct), meters stolen at Khirbet Yarza (14 Oct).
stations.source: Mukhlis Masa'id, Yarza village council via WAFA

stations.subject: Village water networks
stations.what: of the water put into al-Lubban ash-Sharqiya's network is lost before it reaches homes.

stations.subject: Town networks and wastewater
stations.what: of Beit Ula's water is lost in its network; the Kharas wastewater plant is still not running.

stations.subject: Water and sanitation incidents
stations.what: incidents hit water and sanitation infrastructure in September; partners laid or repaired 32 km of network.

stations.subject: Solid waste dumps
stations.what: the Feras Market temporary dump was cleared in September; collection still relies on donkey carts and UN trucks.

stations.subject: AirAware air sensors
stations.what: air-quality stations launched with a public data platform. No reading or update has been published since.

stations.subject: Illegal waste dumps
stations.what: the entrance to a dump used for smuggled waste was blocked with three barriers.

stations.subject: Landfills and climate plan
stations.what: costed measures in Palestine's third climate plan, launched 19 Oct; a $25m landfill programme was reviewed on 15 Oct.

stations.subject: Desalination plant power
stations.what: OCHA cites 'electricity problems' at the Southern Gaza Desalination Plant as one cause of the water drop.

stations.subject: Fuel, engine oil, spares
stations.what: fuel, engine oil and generator parts are short; dialysis and cancer care are at risk.

stations.subject: Cooking gas
stations.what: a kilo of cooking gas on the black market, against 75 shekels for an 8 kg cylinder from the distributor.
stations.source: WAFA reporter Tareq al-Astal via WAFA

stations.subject: Village power lines
stations.what: a Beita family without power after settler cuts; al-Masoudiya was cut for the fifth time on 12 Oct.
stations.source: Mohammed Hamayel, Beita activist; Palestinian Bar Association via WAFA

stations.subject: Village power lines
stations.what: homes cut off when settlers severed the lines, the sixth time in a row.
stations.source: Farid Burqan, Birin village council via WAFA

stations.subject: Solar plant for water pumps
stations.what: of land handed to the Water Authority for a solar plant to power its pumping stations.

stations.subject: Communicable disease
stations.what: of consultations, 4–10 Oct, were for communicable disease; WHO warns of winter outbreaks.

stations.subject: Essential medicines
stations.what: of essential medicines at zero stock; half the laboratory equipment is destroyed.
stations.source: Medical sources in Gaza via WAFA

stations.subject: Hospitals working
stations.what: hospitals and field hospitals partly working, 1 Jan–30 Sep; WHO counts 88 attacks on health care.

stations.subject: Polio (AFP) surveillance
stations.what: acute flaccid paralysis cases this year, to 20 Sept. No surveillance update since.

stations.subject: Mobile medical teams
stations.what: settlers stopped medical teams on the way to Khirbet al-Majaz; 17 Area C locations have no mobile clinic.
